hunks.baseline: Whenever I lost consciousness or fell into a deep sleep, getting caught up in some kind of dream was nothing special anymore.
hunks.sol: Whenever I lost consciousness or fell into a deep sleep, I found myself caught up in some kind of dream. It was nothing unusual anymore.

hunks.baseline: As someone once said, dreams were a window into the mind. Worries I hadn’t managed to shake off and memories that still lingered would get mixed and mashed together, then surface as the illusion we called a dream.
hunks.sol: Someone once said dreams were a window into the mind. Worries I hadn’t managed to shake and memories that still lingered would mix together and surface as the illusion we called a dream.

hunks.baseline: In the end, everything in this world had a cause or a reason. Dreams were no different.
hunks.sol: Everything in this world had a cause or a reason. Dreams were no different.

hunks.baseline: I slowly blinked in the blur of my vision.
hunks.sol: I blinked slowly. My vision was a blur.

hunks.baseline: Unlike my other dreams, which had been horrifyingly vivid, I couldn’t even make out the illusions around me.
hunks.sol: Unlike my other dreams, which had been horrifyingly vivid, I couldn’t even make out the shapes around me.

hunks.baseline: But when someone’s voice suddenly reached me, I finally understood the source of this haze.
hunks.sol: Then someone spoke, and I finally understood why I felt so groggy.

hunks.baseline: *You look awfully sleepy, kid.*
hunks.sol: “Looks like you’re awfully sleepy, little guy.”

hunks.baseline: As the realization finally sank in, I lifted my head.
hunks.sol: As the realization sank in, I lifted my head.

hunks.baseline: No—“my head was lifted” might be more accurate.
hunks.sol: No—*my head lifted* might be more accurate.

hunks.baseline: The eyes that had been blinking from the start, that movement of my head, and even the voice slipping between my lips now weren’t under my control.
hunks.sol: The blinking of my eyes, the movement of my head, even the voice slipping between my lips now—none of it was under my control.

hunks.baseline: *Yeah. I’m sleepy.*
hunks.sol: “Yeah. I’m sleepy.”

hunks.baseline: A child so young that hearing myself whine didn’t feel strange at all.
hunks.sol: Young enough that hearing myself whine didn’t feel strange at all.

hunks.baseline: That answered one question, but a new one quickly took its place.
hunks.sol: That answered one question, but another took its place.

hunks.baseline: Who was the unfamiliar man whose voice was patiently indulging the child’s whining?
hunks.sol: Who was the unfamiliar man indulging the child’s whining?

hunks.baseline: A voice wasn’t exactly an ID card. I couldn’t be expected to recognize someone the instant I heard them. Still, anyone who showed up in my dreams ought to be familiar to me.
hunks.sol: A voice wasn’t an ID card. I couldn’t expect to recognize someone the instant I heard him. Still, anyone who appeared in my dreams ought to be familiar to me.

hunks.baseline: But everything seemed unfamiliar now.
The voice reaching me through my blurry vision. The illusion playing back in slow motion, like a TV screen full of static.
hunks.sol: But everything here was strange. The voice coming through the haze. The scene playing out slowly, like a TV screen full of static.

hunks.baseline: And when I heard the child’s words slip between lips that weren’t mine, I understood where this strange sense of unfamiliarity came from.
hunks.sol: Then I heard the child speak again through lips that weren’t mine, and I understood where that strangeness came from.

hunks.baseline: *Dad. Can I go to sleep?*
hunks.sol: “Dad. Can I go to sleep?”

hunks.baseline: If I’d been able to speak of my own accord, I would’ve let out a groan without realizing it.
hunks.sol: If I’d been able to speak of my own accord, I would have groaned.

hunks.baseline: The truth I’d stumbled across was that astonishing—and that hard to understand.
hunks.sol: What I’d just realized was that startling—and that hard to understand.

hunks.baseline: I could turn over and shake out the oldest drawer of my memories, and still find no memory like this.
hunks.sol: I could turn the oldest drawer of my memories upside down and shake it, and I still wouldn’t find a memory like this.

hunks.baseline: The voice of my father that remained in my mind, however faint, was nothing like the man’s voice coming through my hazy vision.
hunks.sol: The faint memory I had of my father’s voice sounded nothing like the man I was hearing now.

hunks.baseline: So this was—
hunks.sol: Which meant this was—

hunks.baseline: Just then, an inexplicable chill ran down my spine.
hunks.sol: A chill ran down my spine.

hunks.baseline: The unfamiliar man, the one the child had called Dad, spoke into my ear.
hunks.sol: Then the unfamiliar man the child had called Dad spoke close to my ear.

hunks.baseline: *Have a good dream, son.*
hunks.sol: “Have a good dream, my son.”

hunks.baseline: As my vision plunged into darkness, the man’s final words rang faintly in my ears.
hunks.sol: As my vision plunged into darkness, the man’s final word echoed faintly.

hunks.baseline: A father’s voice speaking to his son. His son’s name.
hunks.sol: A father speaking to his son. Calling him by name.

hunks.baseline: And at that moment, my thoughts ground to a halt with the shock of something I’d never expected.
hunks.sol: My thoughts stopped with the shock of it.

hunks.baseline: Fwoosh.
hunks.sol: *Fwoosh.*

hunks.baseline: Light poured down from beyond the pitch-black darkness, wrapping around the child lost in deep sleep.
hunks.sol: Light poured down through the pitch-black darkness, wrapping around the child as he fell into a deep sleep.

hunks.baseline: If someone asked what I saw first whenever I regained consciousness, I’d say the ceiling.
hunks.sol: If someone asked me what I usually saw first when I regained consciousness, I’d say the ceiling.

hunks.baseline: Or Hyuk Mujin, snoring in a corner of the room under the pretense of standing guard. Or Jeok Cheongang, who’d stayed by my side until I woke up.
hunks.sol: Or Hyuk Mujin, snoring in a corner under the pretense of standing guard. Or Jeok Cheongang’s face as he waited by my side for me to wake.

hunks.baseline: But this time, it was none of those.
hunks.sol: This time, it was none of those.

hunks.baseline: I shot upright like a spring and sucked in ragged breaths.
hunks.sol: I sprang upright and gasped for breath.

hunks.baseline: The vision I’d only just regained wavered like melting candle wax, and the voices coming from all around me rang in my ears like thunder.
hunks.sol: My newly regained vision wavered like melting candle wax. Voices from every direction thundered in my ears.

hunks.baseline: “Medicine King…! Come! Hurry!”
hunks.sol: “Medicine King…! Come here! Hurry!”

hunks.baseline: I couldn’t tell one from the other. Caught in confusion, I kept batting away the hands reaching for me on instinct.
hunks.sol: I couldn’t tell. I kept batting away the hands reaching for me, acting on instinct through the confusion.

hunks.baseline: Then someone grabbed me by the shoulder.
hunks.sol: Then someone seized my shoulder.

hunks.baseline: Firmly.
Even in the middle of all that, I could feel the strength in that hand with perfect clarity.
hunks.sol: A powerful grip. Even now, I could feel its strength clearly.

hunks.baseline: A faint pain came with it, along with an unfamiliar warmth.
hunks.sol: It hurt a little, but an unfamiliar warmth came through that hand, too.

hunks.baseline: Shaa…
hunks.sol: *Shaa…*

hunks.baseline: My whole body, tense as a board, slowly relaxed.
hunks.sol: My rigid body slowly relaxed.

hunks.baseline: Only then did I realize whose energy was flowing along the acupoint pathways known to just two people in this vast world—the Extreme Yang qi flowing through me.
hunks.sol: Only then did I recognize the Extreme Yang qi flowing through the acupoint pathways known to just two people in this vast world.

hunks.baseline: “...Old Master.”
hunks.sol: “…Old Master.”

hunks.baseline: At the words I breathed out along with the breath I’d been holding, a voice I knew all too well answered me.
hunks.sol: I let the words out with the breath I’d been holding. A voice I knew all too well answered.

hunks.baseline: I reminded myself that this place I was in was real, not an illusion, and slowly calmed my heart, which was pounding without pause.
hunks.sol: I realized that the place I was in now was real, not a dream, and gradually calmed my racing heart.

hunks.baseline: How much time passed like that?
At last, I opened my eyes and faced a world that was both quiet and clear.
hunks.sol: After a while, I opened my eyes to a world that was quiet and clear.

hunks.baseline: And a familiar face looking at me with concern.
hunks.sol: And to a familiar face watching me with concern.

hunks.baseline: I hesitated a moment before answering his blunt question.
hunks.sol: I hesitated before answering his abrupt question.

hunks.baseline: “So you’re not quite there yet.”
hunks.sol: “So not quite.”

hunks.baseline: “Just once. Don’t hold back at all. Put your whole heart into it.”
hunks.sol: “Just once. Don’t hold back. I mean it.”

hunks.baseline: “Fine. You asked for it.”
hunks.sol: “Fine.”

hunks.baseline: Whoosh.
hunks.sol: *Whoosh.*

hunks.baseline: White flames sprang up in an instant, wrapping around his tightly clenched fist.
hunks.sol: White flames sprang up around his tightly clenched fist.

hunks.baseline: As I watched him prepare to fire off a move from the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist without another word, I calmly spoke up.
hunks.sol: As I watched him prepare to fire off a move from the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist without further discussion, I spoke calmly.

hunks.baseline: “What kind of nonsense is that? The Fire Gate Clan’s martial arts have always been like that.”
hunks.sol: “What kind of nonsense is that? The Fire Gate Clan’s martial arts have always been hot.”

hunks.baseline: “If I can feel how hot it is, I think I’ve definitely come to my senses.”
hunks.sol: “If I can feel the heat, I think I’ve definitely come to my senses.”

hunks.baseline: “I’ve changed my mind. I think I’m all right.”
hunks.sol: “On second thought, I think I’m all right.”

hunks.baseline: “You said to put my whole heart into it.”
hunks.sol: “You told me not to hold back.”

hunks.baseline: “Not quite that much.”
hunks.sol: “Not to this extent.”

hunks.baseline: “Weren’t you the one who asked?”
hunks.sol: “You begged me.”

hunks.baseline: “If you were going to take me that seriously, you should’ve refused three times first. Isn’t that just good manners?”
hunks.sol: “If you were going to take me *that* seriously, you should’ve refused three times first. Isn’t that only polite?”

hunks.baseline: “You lunatic. Do you think I’m Zhuge Cheongang? Quit flapping that mouth and brace yourself.”
hunks.sol: “You lunatic. Do you think I’m Zhuge Cheongang?[^1] Quit flapping that mouth and brace yourself.”

hunks.baseline: “What are you waiting for? Drink something.”
hunks.sol: “What are you waiting for? Drink.”

hunks.baseline: I drained the full bottle in one go without stopping to breathe.
hunks.sol: I drained the full bottle without stopping for breath.

hunks.baseline: The cold water ran down my parched throat, and at last I felt like I could breathe again.
hunks.sol: The cold water ran down my parched throat. At last, I felt like I could breathe again.

hunks.baseline: “...Whoa, I’m awake! Definitely awake! The whole world is beautiful! I’m so happy to be alive!”
hunks.sol: “…Wow, I’m awake! Definitely awake! The whole world is beautiful! I’m so happy to be alive!”

hunks.baseline: “Do you really have to ask? You woke up and immediately started thrashing around like you couldn’t tell up from down, so I sent everyone else out.”
hunks.sol: “Do you really have to ask? You woke up thrashing around like you couldn’t tell up from down. I sent everyone else out.”

hunks.baseline: I’d been overwhelmed by confusion, fighting against the hands trying to hold me back.
hunks.sol: I’d been overwhelmed with confusion and had instinctively fought off the hands trying to hold me.

hunks.baseline: And I had undeniable proof right there in front of me.
hunks.sol: Besides, the proof was right in front of me.

hunks.baseline: I muttered as I looked at the fragments scattered everywhere, their original forms lost. Jeok Cheongang nodded emphatically in agreement.
hunks.sol: I looked at the shattered fragments of what had once been furnishings. Jeok Cheongang nodded emphatically.

hunks.baseline: “It’s a hell of a mess.”
hunks.sol: “A hell of a mess.”

hunks.baseline: “You’re half right and half wrong.”
hunks.sol: “Half right, half wrong.”

hunks.baseline: “Your eldest brother was the one who made a scene. Built like a mountain, bawling his eyes out and insisting he couldn’t leave. I had no choice but to deal with him myself.”
hunks.sol: “Your eldest brother made a scene. Built like a mountain, bawling his eyes out, insisting he wouldn’t leave. I had no choice but to deal with him myself.”

hunks.baseline: A long time ago, I would’ve been clutching my ass, which came equipped with a built-in stick of dynamite, and counting down. Not anymore.
hunks.sol: A long time ago, I would’ve clutched my ass like it came with built-in dynamite and started counting down. Not anymore.

hunks.baseline: I gave a quiet laugh without answering. Jeok Cheongang clicked his tongue.
hunks.sol: I gave a quiet laugh instead of answering. Jeok Cheongang clicked his tongue.

hunks.baseline: “Come on, you’re always snapping at me. You know I know better.”
hunks.sol: “Come on, you’re sulking again. You know that’s not true.”

hunks.baseline: “Know what, my ass. More importantly… what caused this?”
hunks.sol: “Know what, my ass. More importantly… what was it?”

hunks.baseline: The question came with a brief pause, his voice trailing off.
hunks.sol: His voice trailed off before the short question.

hunks.baseline: I opened my mouth, feeling the sweat that had soaked my back.
hunks.sol: I felt cold sweat soaking my back.

hunks.baseline: “What sort of nightmare was it?”
hunks.sol: “What sort of nightmare?”

hunks.baseline: “No, I wouldn’t call it a nightmare… I don’t know. It was a strange dream I can’t really describe.”
hunks.sol: “No, it wasn’t exactly a nightmare… I don’t know. It was a strange dream. I can’t really describe it.”

hunks.baseline: Even as I answered, an odd feeling crept over me. I frowned.
hunks.sol: Even as I answered, something about the situation felt odd. I frowned.

hunks.baseline: *What is this?*
hunks.sol: *What is it?*

hunks.baseline: The situation felt strangely familiar.
hunks.sol: It felt strangely familiar.

hunks.baseline: But the sense of déjà vu that had come over me vanished when Jeok Cheongang spoke again, his voice grave.
hunks.sol: But the sudden sense of déjà vu vanished when Jeok Cheongang spoke again, his voice grave.

hunks.baseline: “Tell me more. That nightmare might have been a trace of the Heart Demon inside you.”
hunks.sol: “Tell me more. That nightmare could be a trace of the Heart Demon lurking inside you.”

hunks.baseline: I pushed aside my brief hesitation and answered.
hunks.sol: I put aside my brief hesitation.

hunks.baseline: “I don’t think so. It was just a memory.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t think so. It was a memory.”

hunks.baseline: “Even an unhappy memory can leave a trace of the Heart Demon. I’ve seen people who were trapped by such a past until it brought them to ruin.”
hunks.sol: “An unhappy memory can leave a trace of the Heart Demon, too. I’ve seen people trapped by their past until it destroyed them.”

hunks.baseline: For a Murim martial artist to break past their limits and reach the highest realms, powerful internal energy and martial arts weren’t enough.
hunks.sol: For a Murim martial artist to break past their limits and reach a higher realm, powerful internal energy and martial arts weren’t enough. They also needed the enlightenment gained by training the mind.

hunks.baseline: They needed spiritual insight gained through training the mind.

hunks.baseline: Whether good or evil, they had to gain an understanding of their own before they could keep walking that path.
hunks.sol: Whether their path was good or evil, they had to reach an understanding of their own to keep walking it.

hunks.baseline: And for anyone who’d begun that mental training, an illness of the heart left untreated could be devastating.
hunks.sol: And for those who had begun that training, an unhealed illness of the mind could be devastating.

hunks.baseline: *Like how Old Master suffered from the infirmities of old age after losing Jopil. No—Jangcheon.*
hunks.sol: *Like Old Master suffering from the infirmities of old age after losing Jopil. No—Jangcheon.*

hunks.baseline: That was why Jeok Cheongang’s serious concern wasn’t an overreaction at all.
hunks.sol: So Jeok Cheongang’s concern wasn’t an overreaction.

hunks.baseline: People knew the Fire King Jeok Cheongang for a temper like hellfire, but beneath that burned the caution and wisdom he’d honed over a lifetime.
hunks.sol: The world knew the Fire King Jeok Cheongang for a temper like hellfire. But inside him lay the caution and wisdom honed over many long years.

hunks.baseline: But this time, I could answer his concern without hesitation.
hunks.sol: This time, though, I could answer him without hesitation.

hunks.baseline: I met Jeok Cheongang’s gaze as his expression hardened, then continued slowly.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang’s expression hardened. I met his gaze and slowly continued.

hunks.baseline: I swallowed a breath that had begun to tremble.
hunks.sol: I swallowed a trembling breath.

hunks.baseline: And at the same time, I remembered.
The man’s voice, faintly seeping into the ear of a child falling into a deep sleep in that hazy dream.
hunks.sol: And I remembered the man’s voice, faintly reaching the child as he fell into a deep sleep in that hazy dream.

hunks.baseline: *Have a good dream, my son… Taekyung.*
hunks.sol: “Have a good dream, my son… Taekyung.”
[^1]: Zhuge Liang, the famed strategist, was courted through three visits before agreeing to serve.
